The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=54) (I4) and healthy controls; group sizes exceed the minimum (I5). The paper reports between-group voxelwise contrasts and whole-brain regression results in MNI space (I6, I7) and describes results in text/tables/supplement (I8). Full text contains methods, results, and imaging details allowing extraction of voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for this review.

This is an empirical VBM study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=12) with voxelwise, whole-brain permutation-based analyses. T1 images were normalized to MNI space and group-level between-group contrasts (patients vs. controls) and voxelwise regressions relating behavior to gray matter density are reported. Sample sizes meet the minimum (patients and controls), and whole-brain voxelwise results are presented (clusters reported). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not a review, not ROI-only, not only FC/DTI/thickness). Therefore it satisfies all required inclusion criteria.

This study meets inclusion criteria: it used VBM (optimized VBM on MRI) and FDG-PET (I3); the FTD sample (n=13) were clinically diagnosed using Neary consensus criteria and semantic dementia and progressive nonfluent aphasia were excluded, indicating the sample corresponds to behavioral-variant FTD rather than language variants (I4) — although the paper does not explicitly use the term “bvFTD,” the diagnostic approach and exclusions support this classification. Sample size meets minimum (13 FTD patients; I5). Analyses were whole-brain, voxelwise using SPM2 with normalization to MNI space and reported group-level voxelwise contrasts and figures/tables (I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses 18FDG-PET (I3); includes clinically diagnosed frontal-variant FTLD patients (fv-FTLD), corresponding to behavioral variant FTD (I4); has adequate sample sizes (18 patients; 24 controls; PET subset ≥6) (I5); reports voxelwise between-group contrasts in MNI space using SPM (I6); provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results for the target patient groups (I7); and reports coordinates/figures consistent with acceptable reporting (I8). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper is an empirical PET study (not a review), contains whole-brain analyses (not ROI-only), excludes patients with major depression/alcohol abuse per methods, and does not use only FC/DTI/cortical thickness methods. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Exclusion: E4 met — study sample includes 3 patients with mild associated signs of motor neuron disease (a concurrent neurological symptom), which meets exclusion criterion E4. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET used), I4 (clinically diagnosed FTD patients consistent with bvFTD; primary progressive aphasia and semantic dementia were excluded), I5 (n=29 patients; >6), I6 (reports between-group contrasts in MNI space), I7 (reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level conjunction results), I8 (coordinates reported in text/figures). No inclusion criteria unmet. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded due to E4.

This is an empirical study that includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=21) and uses resting-state fMRI and VBM (meets imaging modality). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (group ICA and dual regression) were performed and reported in MNI space (voxelwise results and coordinates discussed), and at least one between-group contrast (bvFTD vs controls) is reported. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review, ROI-only, non-empirical, seed-only/DTI) apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8. Full text appears complete.

This study reports empirical resting-state fMRI and VBM analyses in a clinical sample of 19 bvFTD patients and 19 controls. It uses whole-brain ICA dual-regression and voxelwise permutation testing (FSL randomize with TFCE) and reports voxelwise between-group contrasts with MNI coordinates and tables/figures. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (>=6). The paper includes full Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not DTI/seed-only, and sample is clinically diagnosed bvFTD). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical lesion-imaging study that satisfies all inclusion criteria. It includes voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and resting-state fMRI analyses (I3). The sample contains clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=26) (I4) and meets the minimum sample size (I5). The paper reports between-group voxelwise contrasts and structural atrophy coordinates derived using SPM/DARTEL normalized to MNI space (I6), with whole-brain, group-level VBM results clearly presented for the bvFTD group (I7). Coordinate results are reported in figures and supplementary tables (I8). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met.

This empirical study used FDG-PET with voxel-based (SPM8) whole-brain analyses, included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=26) and controls/AD, and reports voxelwise between-group contrasts normalized to MNI space (SPM, reported cluster/BA results and supplementary tables). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results are clearly described (bvFTD vs HC; amnestic vs non-amnestic bvFTD) and correlations between FCSRT scores and metabolism are reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria: it uses FDG-PET (I3); includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=19) (I4); sample sizes exceed the minimum (I5); reports voxel-based, whole-brain voxelwise analyses normalized to MNI space with group-level results and correlations reported for the bvFTD group (voxel-based brain mapping and Supplementary Table S2) satisfying between-group/ group-level voxelwise result requirement (I6, I7); results are presented in figures and supplementary tables/coordinates (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: it is an empirical study with whole-brain voxelwise results (E2, E3, E5, E6 not applicable) and there is no indication of disqualifying psychiatric comorbidity or only ROI/seed-based analyses. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Supplementary Materials referenced).

This is an empirical longitudinal study that includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=12) and uses resting-state fMRI and voxel-based morphometry (VBM). The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise group-level contrasts (dual regression ICA and voxel-wise analyses) using standard space registration (MNI) with FWE-corrected results, and presents cross-sectional and longitudinal whole-brain findings for bvFTD versus controls and AD. Sample sizes meet the minimum (bvFTD n=12; controls n=22). Whole-brain voxelwise results are reported in the text/figures/tables. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7,I8) are met. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This empirical resting-state fMRI study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=8) and healthy controls (n=16), meeting sample-size requirements. Imaging modalities include resting-state fMRI and voxel-based morphometry for gray-matter correction. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts with coordinate reporting (e.g., BA46 peak at x=36,y=42,z=30), and presents group-level whole-brain results and brain–behavior covariates. All required inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7,I8) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, includes whole-brain analyses, excludes comorbid psychiatric/neurological conditions, is empirical, and is not limited to only seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=35) (I4) with adequate sample sizes (bvFTD n=35, controls n=29) (I5), reports voxel-wise between-group contrasts and VBM correlations in MNI space with peak coordinates referenced in Supplementary Table 3 (I6), and provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results identified for the bvFTD sample (I7). Coordinate results are reported in text/tables (I8). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text is complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical VBM study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=34) with healthy controls (n=30). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise VBM analyses comparing patient subgroups and controls (FDR-corrected results are described; Supplementary Table/Figure referenced for whole-brain coordinates), provides methods for stereotaxic normalization and voxelwise statistics, and reports between-group contrasts and associated anatomical coordinates in supplementary materials. Sample sizes exceed the minimum. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets imaging modality (VBM), clinical sample, sample size, between-group voxelwise results in stereotaxic space (via reported supplementary tables), and whole-brain evidence.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses VBM (SPM99) (I3); includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients with behavioral symptoms consistent with behavioral-variant FTD and explicitly excluded primary aphasias (I4); sample size is 9 FTD patients and 26 controls (meets I5); reports voxelwise, whole-brain SPM results and provides stereotactic coordinates (e.g., (0, -28, -10)) (I6); presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results clearly attributed to the patient group (I7); and whole-brain results are reported in the text/figures/tables (I8). No exclusion criteria are met (no review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, empirical VBM study, no disallowed modalities). Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an original empirical study that uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and FDG-PET imaging, includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=23; n=21 in MRI analysis after QC), reports whole-brain voxelwise SPM results with stereotactic coordinates converted between MNI and Talairach, and presents group-level voxelwise comparisons vs. controls and vs. bipolar disorder. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical FDG-PET study using voxel-wise SPM analysis (whole-brain) of 29 clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia patients (specified as FTD and excluding PNFA/semantic dementia), and 11 healthy controls. It reports group-level voxelwise between-group contrasts with MNI/Talairach coordinates (Table 3) and whole-brain SPM results (figures and tables). Sample sizes exceed the minimum. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8.

The study used FDG-PET (I3), included 25 FTD patients (and 9 SD) meeting Lund-Manchester clinical criteria with clinical features described consistent with behavioral-variant FTD, satisfying I4. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (I5). Voxelwise SPM analysis reported whole-brain between-group contrasts with Talairach coordinates and cluster-level results (I6, I7, I8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and is complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

Meets all inclusion criteria for the review. The study used 18F-FDG PET (I3), included clinically diagnosed FTD patients per Lund-Manchester criteria and excluded semantic and non-fluent variants (consistent with bvFTD sample; I4), had n=29 patients and n=16 controls (I5), reports voxelwise, whole-brain SPM analyses with reported Talairach coordinates (I6, I7) and presents coordinates and figures describing whole-brain results (I8). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it includes clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD patients (n=12) (I4), uses FDG-PET as an imaging modality alongside ASL (I3), has adequate sample size (≥6 in patient group) (I5), reports voxel-wise between-group contrasts using SPM normalized to MNI space with MNI coordinates and cluster tables/figures (I6, I7, I8). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results are described and projected on MNI brain; ROI analyses are present but do not replace the reported whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, empirical original data, not limited to excluded modalities). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, multi-center VBM study using SPM/VBM8 with MNI normalization that compares 52 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients to 52 healthy controls. It reports voxelwise, whole-brain group contrasts (FWE-corrected) with MNI coordinates and figures, and provides full methods, results, and discussion. Sample sizes exceed the minimum. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical study of clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) that uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts with MNI coordinates. Sample sizes meet the minimum (bvFTD N=26 overall; MRI subset N=21 bvFTD, controls N=12). The paper provides whole-brain VBM results (FDR-corrected) and tables/figures with MNI coordinates linking regional atrophy to behavioural measures. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies all listed inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This empirical study met all required inclusion criteria: it investigated behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) patients, used voxel-based morphometry (MRI VBM) and 18F-FDG PET (I3), included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (selected as patients who converted to probable bvFTD; I4), had adequate sample sizes (25 patients, 20 controls; I5), and reported voxelwise, whole-brain between-group contrasts with Talairach-coordinate tables and SPM analyses (I6, I7, I8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (E2, E3, E4, E5, E6) are triggered: the paper is primary empirical work, reports whole-brain voxelwise results (not ROI-only or seed-based FC/DTI/cortical-thickness-only), and excluded participants with major psychiatric/other neurological disorders. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study is an empirical, task-based fMRI investigation of music and vocal emotion processing in clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=15) versus healthy controls (n=11). It reports between-group voxelwise contrasts analyzed in SPM with normalization to MNI space and presents group-level whole-brain results (e.g., musical mode variation: controls > bvFTD, P < 0.05 FWE whole-brain) as well as small-volume corrected findings. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets the review’s imaging modality requirement (task fMRI), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample, satisfies the sample size threshold, reports between-group contrasts in MNI space, and provides at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise result from the target sample. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical VBM study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (Rascovsky criteria) with adequate sample sizes (25 patients, 20 controls). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise VBM group comparisons and TBSS DTI analyses after normalizing images to MNI space, with results presented in figures and supplementary tables (whole-brain coordinates reported in supplementary material). Thus it meets all required inclusion criteria (VBM modality, bvFTD sample, n>=6, between-group contrasts in MNI space, and whole-brain group-level voxelwise results). No exclusion criteria apply: this is not a review, not ROI-only, participants with psychiatric comorbidity were excluded, and the study includes VBM (not only DTI or FC). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).
